$comment: CodeQL findings we've read and accepted, by rule and file. `filter-sarif.sh` drops them before upload, so they never become alerts and never block. Each needs a reason a reviewer can check. A new finding of the same rule in the same file is accepted too, so keep entries to files where the rule can't apply.

accepted.reason: The `AWS4` / `GOOG4` key prefixes are fixed by the SigV4 spec: the signing key is HMAC(prefix + secret, date). The secret itself comes from the user's profile.

Both the value and its use point at the `ipc_command_manifest!(build_invoke_handler)` call in `builder()`, which expands to `tauri::generate_handler!` over every command: the finding lives in macro-generated dispatch code. The file holds no secret literal.
An SMB guest sign-in is the `Guest` user with an empty password by protocol; it's the fallback when the user gave no credentials.
Linux-only module (`#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]`), so the macOS-target analysis can't see its `#[cfg(test)]` module as test code; the flagged passwords are that module's test inputs.
`fingerprint` is a truncated SHA-256 of an API key, used to tell keys apart in the UI and logs. It isn't password storage; the key itself lives in the Keychain.
The `account_id` it flags is the Cloudflare R2 account id, which is part of the endpoint hostname by design (`<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`). It's an identifier, not a credential.
Dev-only launcher. It logs the dev data dir and instance id, which derive from `XDG_DATA_HOME` and `CMDR_INSTANCE_ID`; CodeQL treats all of `process.env` as sensitive.
Dev-only helper of `tauri-wrapper.ts`. It logs a port-file path under the dev data dir, which derives from `XDG_DATA_HOME`; CodeQL treats all of `process.env` as sensitive.
